page: Amazon Web Services c8i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs, corresponding to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading, operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor configuration includes a 480 MB L3 cache, a 2 MB L2 cache, and a 48 KB L1d cache. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps and does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance across CPU-bound and cryptographic operations. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 51718.7 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 18229.0, placing both in the top 25% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 34.25 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performed at 227.98 GB/sec. For language model workloads, the server demonstrated top-tier performance in text generation using a small 135M model at 357.67 tokens/second. Memory bandwidth tests showed 2560.7 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 178.37 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c8i.8xlarge offers high compute density and advanced instruction support, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for vector and matrix operations. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and integrated GPUs represents a clear tradeoff, requiring external block storage for persistent data and limiting its suitability for heavy graphics or large-scale GPU-accelerated deep learning. This hardware profile is highly suited for compute-heavy workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, text and image processing, and small-to-medium LLM inference tasks.
